# HRMS - Human Resource Management System

## Overview

This HRMS (Human Resource Management System) is a full-stack web application managing the entire employee lifecycle: recruitment, employee management, attendance, leave, expense claims, performance, and payroll. It is designed as a modern enterprise SaaS platform, inspired by BambooHR and Workday, focusing on clarity, efficient workflows, and a professional aesthetic. The system features Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) with distinct experiences for System Admin, HR Manager, Department Manager, and Employee roles. The primary color for branding is blue (#1965ae).

## User Preferences

Preferred communication style: Simple, everyday language.

## Documentation

Comprehensive technical documentation is available in the `/docs` folder and project root:

- **README.md**: Project overview, features, quick start, tech stack
- **docs/TECHNICAL_DOCUMENTATION.md**: Complete technical reference including architecture, database schema, API reference, authentication, and module documentation
- **docs/SITE_MAP.md**: Visual site map with route structure and access control matrix
- **docs/USER_GUIDE.md**: Role-specific walkthroughs, module guides, common tasks, and FAQs
- **docs/QUICK_START.md**: Developer and System Administrator quick start guides

## Recent Changes

### November 22, 2025 - Navigation Highlighting & Complete Documentation
- **Navigation Improvements**
  - Fixed sidebar navigation highlighting using longest-match-first algorithm
  - Updated sidebar accent colors to use primary blue (#1965ae) for active states
  - Active navigation items now correctly highlight based on current route
  - Works for exact matches and sub-routes (e.g., /admin/devices highlights "Device Configuration")
- **Comprehensive Documentation Created**
  - Generated complete technical documentation covering architecture, database schema, API reference
  - Created visual site map with route structure and RBAC access matrix
  - Developed user guide with role-specific walkthroughs and FAQs
  - Added quick start guides for developers and system administrators
  - Updated README.md with project overview and setup instructions
- **Files modified**: client/src/index.css, client/src/components/app-sidebar.tsx
- **Files created**: README.md, docs/TECHNICAL_DOCUMENTATION.md, docs/SITE_MAP.md, docs/USER_GUIDE.md, docs/QUICK_START.md

### November 21, 2025 - Enhanced Device Management & Attendance Filtering
- **Device Management Enhancements**
  - Added delete device functionality with confirmation dialog on device cards
  - Fixed navigation: back/cancel buttons in device configuration now properly route to `/admin/devices`
  - Implemented real TCP connection testing with multiple states (idle, testing, success, failed, timeout)
  - Added ZKTeco API mode support with script input textarea and file import (.js, .json, .txt, .xml)
  - Connection test displays detailed feedback messages for all result states
- **Attendance Filtering System**
  - Added comprehensive filter controls to Attendance Records view
  - Time period selector: Today, This Week, This Month, Last Week, Last Month, Custom Range
  - Custom date range picker with from/to calendar selectors
  - Department, Location, and Company filter dropdowns
  - Reset filters button for quick filter clearing
- **UI/UX Improvements**
  - Fixed dropdown contrast issue: SelectItem components now have bg-popover background with hover-elevate
  - Improved visual feedback for connection testing states
  - Enhanced device card layout with delete icon button
- **Files modified**: client/src/pages/admin/devices.tsx, client/src/pages/device-configuration.tsx, client/src/pages/attendance.tsx, client/src/components/ui/select.tsx

### November 21, 2025 - Device Configuration Moved to Admin Portal
- **Restructured ZKTeco device management** to be admin-only feature
  - Created dedicated Device Configuration page at `/admin/devices` for System Admin role
  - Removed "Devices" tab from Attendance page (now shows only Attendance Records and Calendar View)
  - Updated routing: device management routes moved from `/attendance/device/*` to `/admin/device/*`
  - Added proper RBAC guards using RequireRole component to restrict access to system_admin
  - Architect-verified: RequireRole component correctly enforces role-based access control
- **Security**: Device configuration, sync operations, and device addition now restricted to System Admin only
- **Navigation**: Device Configuration menu item in admin sidebar points to `/admin/devices`
- **Files modified**: client/src/pages/admin/devices.tsx (new), client/src/App.tsx, client/src/pages/attendance.tsx, client/src/components/app-sidebar.tsx

## System Architecture

### Frontend Architecture

The frontend is built with React, TypeScript, Vite, Wouter for routing, TanStack Query for data fetching, and Tailwind CSS for styling. It leverages `shadcn/ui` components based on Radix UI for accessibility and customizability, implementing a professional design system with Poppins typography, consistent spacing, and a 0.8rem border radius. State management primarily uses React Query for server state and local React state for UI interactions. The layout is responsive, featuring a fixed sidebar for desktop and a collapsible drawer for mobile.

### Backend Architecture

The backend uses Node.js with Express and TypeScript, organized around RESTful API endpoints. It distinguishes between development (Vite middleware) and production (static asset serving) modes. A custom logging utility tracks requests and responses.

### Authentication & Authorization

Authentication is handled via local email/password using Passport Local Strategy, with user sessions stored in PostgreSQL. Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) is production-ready, featuring four tiers: `system_admin`, `hr_manager`, `department_manager`, and `employee`. Backend middleware (`requireRole`) and frontend route guards (`RequireRole` component) enforce permissions. Security hardening includes multi-layer CSRF protection, secure HTTP-only cookies, and bcrypt hashing for passwords. The system includes an Admin Configuration module for user, department, leave type, and expense category management, with automated credential emails sent via Resend.

### Data Layer

PostgreSQL is the primary database, connected via Neon Serverless driver and Drizzle ORM for type-safe queries. The schema is defined centrally in `shared/schema.ts`, managed with Drizzle Kit. Key data models include Users, Employees, Departments, Attendance, Leave, Expenses, Recruitment, Performance, and Sessions. An abstract `IStorage` interface defines data access patterns, implemented using Drizzle ORM for CRUD operations.

### Module Organization

The system is organized into feature modules: Recruitment, Employees, Attendance, Leave, Expenses, Performance, Payroll, Reports, Settings, and System Admin. The codebase is structured into `/client` (React app), `/server` (Express app), and `/shared` (types/schemas), with path aliases for clean imports.

## External Dependencies

### Database & Infrastructure
- **PostgreSQL**: Primary relational database.
- **Neon Serverless**: Database connectivity.

### Authentication
- **Passport Local Strategy**: For local email/password authentication.
- **Bcrypt**: For password hashing.

### UI Component Libraries
- **Radix UI primitives**: Foundation for accessible components.
- **Lucide React**: Icon system.

### Utility Libraries
- **date-fns**: Date manipulation.
- **clsx**, **tailwind-merge**: CSS class composition.
- **Zod**: Runtime validation.
- **React Hook Form**: Form management with Zod resolvers.
- **Nanoid**: Unique ID generation.

### Email Service
- **Resend**: Transactional email service for credential notifications.

### Biometric Integration
- **ZKTeco protocol**: (Planned) for attendance device integration.

# HRMS Design Guidelines

## Design Approach
**System-Based Approach** inspired by BambooHR and Workday's enterprise SaaS interfaces, emphasizing information clarity, efficient workflows, and professional aesthetics for data-intensive HR operations.

## Core Design Principles
1. **Information Density with Breathing Room** - Dense data displays balanced with generous whitespace
2. **Workflow Efficiency** - Minimize clicks, streamline multi-step processes
3. **Role-Based Clarity** - Clear visual differentiation between admin, manager, and employee views
4. **Trust & Professionalism** - Conservative, reliable aesthetic appropriate for HR data

## Typography System (Poppins Family)

**Hierarchy:**
- Page Titles: 2rem (32px), font-weight 600
- Section Headers: 1.5rem (24px), font-weight 600
- Card Titles: 1.125rem (18px), font-weight 600
- Body Text: 0.875rem (14px), font-weight 400
- Labels/Meta: 0.75rem (12px), font-weight 500, uppercase tracking-wide
- Data Tables: 0.8125rem (13px), font-weight 400

**Line Heights:** 1.5 for body text, 1.2 for headings

## Layout System

**Spacing Primitives (Tailwind):**
Primary units: 2, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16
- Component padding: p-4 to p-6
- Card spacing: p-6 (desktop), p-4 (mobile)
- Section gaps: gap-6 or gap-8
- Page margins: px-6 lg:px-8
- Vertical rhythm: space-y-6 between major sections

**Grid System:**
- Dashboard cards: 3-column grid (lg:grid-cols-3), 2-column (md:grid-cols-2), 1-column (mobile)
- Data tables: Full-width with horizontal scroll on mobile
- Forms: 2-column layout (md:grid-cols-2) with full-width textareas
- Sidebar: Fixed 256px width (desktop), collapsible drawer (mobile)

**Border Radius:** 0.8rem consistently across all cards, buttons, and form inputs

## Navigation Architecture

**Sidebar Navigation (Desktop):**
- Fixed left sidebar, 256px width
- Grouped menu items by module (Recruitment, Employees, Attendance, Leave, Expenses, Performance, Payroll, Reports)
- Active state: Background fill with primary color at 10% opacity
- Icon + label pattern for all items
- Collapsible sub-menus for nested features

**Top Bar:**
- Full-width header with breadcrumb navigation
- Right-aligned: Notifications bell, user profile dropdown
- Height: 64px

**Mobile Navigation:**
- Hamburger menu triggering slide-out drawer
- Bottom navigation bar for primary modules (optional for key features)

## Component Library

### Cards
- Background: hsl(0, 0%, 99%) white
- Border: 1px solid hsl(0, 0%, 90%)
- Shadow: subtle (shadow-sm), elevated on hover (shadow-md transition)
- Padding: p-6
- Header with title + optional action button in top-right

### Buttons
**Primary:** Background primary color, white text, px-6 py-2.5
**Secondary:** Border with primary color, primary text, px-6 py-2.5
**Ghost:** Transparent background, primary text, hover state with 5% background
**Icon Buttons:** Square 40px, centered icon, subtle hover background

### Forms
- Label above input, font-size 0.75rem, font-weight 500
- Input fields: h-10, px-4, border neutral grey, focus ring with primary color
- Full-width by default, 2-column grid for related fields
- Required fields: Red asterisk after label
- Helper text: 0.75rem below input, neutral grey
- Validation: Red border + error message for invalid states

### Data Tables
- Striped rows (alternate background hsl(0, 0%, 98%))
- Header: Background hsl(0, 0%, 96%), font-weight 600, sticky on scroll
- Cell padding: px-4 py-3
- Row hover: Background hsl(0, 0%, 97%)
- Actions column: Right-aligned with icon buttons
- Pagination: Bottom-right, showing "1-20 of 150 results"
- Mobile: Horizontal scroll wrapper with sticky first column

### Modals
- Centered overlay with semi-transparent backdrop
- Max-width: 640px (md) to 896px (lg) depending on content
- Close button: Top-right, icon only
- Footer with action buttons: Right-aligned, Cancel (secondary) + Primary action

### Tabs
- Horizontal tabs with underline indicator (3px height, primary color)
- Tab padding: px-4 py-3
- Active tab: Primary color text, bold weight
- Inactive: Neutral grey text, hover state

### Status Badges
- Small pill-shaped indicators (px-3 py-1, text-xs, rounded-full)
- Semantic colors: Success (green), Warning (yellow), Error (red), Info (blue), Pending (grey)
- Used in tables, employee cards, approval workflows

### Dashboard Metrics Cards
- Large number display: 2.5rem, font-weight 700
- Label below: 0.875rem, neutral grey
- Optional trend indicator: Small arrow + percentage change
- Icon in top-right corner, primary color at 20% opacity background circle

## Module-Specific Patterns

### Dashboard
- 4-column metrics grid (top section)
- Activity feed + upcoming events (2-column split)
- Quick action buttons for common tasks
- Device status overview for ZKTeco integration (grid of device cards)

### Employee Directory
- List view: Avatar + name + role + department + location (sortable columns)
- Grid view: Card layout with profile photo, name, title, contact button
- Filter sidebar: Department, location, employment type checkboxes

### Attendance Management
- Calendar heatmap view for monthly overview
- Device management table with status indicators (online/offline)
- Real-time sync status with last updated timestamp
- Punch in/out logs table with filters

### Leave Management
- Calendar view showing approved/pending leaves
- Balance summary cards (available/taken/pending)
- Request form with date range picker
- Approval queue for managers with batch actions

### Payroll
- Payslip preview with detailed breakdowns
- Salary component configuration table
- Run payroll wizard (multi-step form)
- Export functionality prominently placed

## Responsive Behavior
- Desktop-first approach with breakpoints: sm (640px), md (768px), lg (1024px), xl (1280px)
- Sidebar collapses to drawer on < lg
- Tables scroll horizontally on mobile with sticky first column
- Form layouts stack to single column on < md
- Dashboard metrics reduce from 4-col to 2-col to 1-col

## Animations
**Minimal and purposeful:**
- Transitions: 150ms ease for hover states, 200ms for modals
- Sidebar drawer: 300ms slide animation
- No scroll-triggered animations
- Loading states: Subtle skeleton screens or spinner

## Images
This enterprise application primarily uses **iconography over photography**. No hero images. Profile photos in employee cards/directory are the main photographic content. Device status dashboards may include small equipment icons/illustrations for visual reference.

## Table of Contents

## Project Overview

### Description
HRMS (Human Resource Management System) is a comprehensive, enterprise-grade web application designed to manage the complete employee lifecycle. The system provides tools for recruitment, employee management, attendance tracking with biometric device integration, leave management, expense claims, performance reviews, and payroll processing.

### Key Features
- **Multi-tenant Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)** with 4 distinct user roles
- **ZKTeco Biometric Integration** for attendance tracking via MB100 devices
- **Real-time Dashboard Analytics** for all user roles
- **Automated Email Notifications** via Resend integration
- **Comprehensive Reporting System** with exportable data
- **Responsive Design** optimized for desktop and mobile
- **Dark/Light Theme Support** with persistent user preferences

### Target Users
- **System Administrators**: Full system configuration and user management
- **HR Managers**: Complete HR operations and workforce management
- **Department Managers**: Team management and approval workflows
- **Employees**: Self-service portal for leave, expenses, and performance tracking

---

## System Architecture

### Architecture Pattern
**Full-Stack Monolithic Architecture** with clear separation of concerns:

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    Client Layer (React)                      │
│  ┌──────────────┐  ┌──────────────┐  ┌──────────────┐      │
│  │   Pages      │  │  Components  │  │    Hooks     │      │
│  └──────────────┘  └──────────────┘  └──────────────┘      │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                            ↕ HTTP/WebSocket
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                   Server Layer (Express)                     │
│  ┌──────────────┐  ┌──────────────┐  ┌──────────────┐      │
│  │  Routes      │  │  Middleware  │  │   Storage    │      │
│  └──────────────┘  └──────────────┘  └──────────────┘      │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                            ↕ SQL/Drizzle ORM
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│              Data Layer (PostgreSQL/Neon)                    │
│  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
│  │  Users, Employees, Attendance, Leave, Expenses, etc. │   │
│  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### Frontend Architecture
- **Framework**: React 18 with TypeScript
- **Routing**: Wouter (lightweight client-side routing)
- **State Management**: 
  - TanStack Query v5 for server state
  - React Context for authentication state
  - Local state for UI interactions
- **Styling**: Tailwind CSS with shadcn/ui component library
- **Forms**: React Hook Form with Zod validation
- **Theme**: next-themes for dark/light mode persistence

### Backend Architecture
- **Framework**: Express.js with TypeScript
- **API Design**: RESTful JSON API
- **Session Management**: express-session with PostgreSQL store
- **Authentication**: Passport.js with Local Strategy
- **ORM**: Drizzle ORM for type-safe database queries
- **Validation**: Zod schemas shared between frontend and backend
- **Email Service**: Resend for transactional emails

### Data Layer
- **Database**: PostgreSQL (Neon Serverless)
- **Schema Management**: Drizzle Kit for migrations
- **Connection Pooling**: Neon serverless driver with auto-scaling
- **Session Store**: connect-pg-simple for PostgreSQL session storage

---

## Technology Stack

### Core Technologies
| Layer | Technology | Version | Purpose |
|-------|-----------|---------|---------|
| Frontend Framework | React | 18.3.1 | UI components and rendering |
| Backend Framework | Express | 4.21.2 | HTTP server and API routes |

| Database | PostgreSQL | Latest | Primary data store |
| ORM | Drizzle ORM | 0.39.1 | Type-safe database queries |
| Build Tool | Vite | 5.4.20 | Frontend build and dev server |

### Frontend Libraries

| wouter | Client-side routing |
| @tanstack/react-query | Server state management and caching |
| react-hook-form | Form state management |
| zod | Runtime type validation |
| @radix-ui/* | Accessible UI primitives |
| lucide-react | Icon system |
| date-fns | Date manipulation |
| recharts | Data visualization |
| framer-motion | Animations |
| next-themes | Theme management |

### Backend Libraries

| passport | Authentication framework |
| passport-local | Email/password authentication |
| bcrypt | Password hashing |
| express-session | Session management |
| connect-pg-simple | PostgreSQL session store |
| drizzle-zod | Zod schema generation from Drizzle |
| resend | Email service integration |

### Development Tools

| esbuild | Production build bundler |

---

## Database Schema

### Entity Relationship Overview

```
users (authentication)
  ├── employees (employee records)
  │     ├── attendanceLogs
  │     ├── leaveRequests
  │     ├── expenseClaims
  │     ├── performanceGoals
  │     ├── appraisals
  │     ├── salaryConfigs
  │     └── payrollRecords
  ├── departments
  ├── employeeRequests
  └── feedback

departments
  ├── employees
  └── jobPostings
        └── candidates

attendanceDevices
  └── attendanceLogs

leaveTypes
  └── leaveRequests

expenseCategories
  └── expenseClaims
```

### Core Tables

#### users
Authentication and system access control.
```typescript
- id: varchar (UUID, primary key)
- email: varchar (unique)
- firstName: varchar
- lastName: varchar
- profileImageUrl: varchar
- passwordHash: varchar (bcrypt hashed)
- role: enum (system_admin, hr_manager, department_manager, employee)
- departmentId: varchar (foreign key)
- createdAt: timestamp
- updatedAt: timestamp
```

#### employees
Employee master records.

```typescript
- id: varchar (UUID, primary key)
- userId: varchar (foreign key to users, nullable)
- firstName: text
- lastName: text
- email: text (unique)
- phone: text
- departmentId: varchar (foreign key)
- role: text (job title)
- biometricId: text (unique, for device integration)
- status: enum (active, inactive, terminated)

```

Organizational structure.


```typescript
- port: text (default: "4370")

- branch: text
- status: enum (online, offline)
- lastSyncAt: timestamp

```

Daily attendance records.

```typescript
- checkIn: timestamp
- checkOut: timestamp
- date: date

```

#### leaveTypes

```typescript
- daysAllowed: integer
- createdAt: timestamp
```

#### leaveRequests
Employee leave applications.
```typescript
- id: varchar (UUID, primary key)
- employeeId: varchar (foreign key)
- leaveTypeId: varchar (foreign key)
- fromDate: date
- toDate: date
- days: integer
- reason: text
```

## Authentication & Authorization

### Authentication Flow

1. **User Login**
   - User submits email and password
   - Server validates credentials using bcrypt
   - Passport.js creates session
   - Session stored in PostgreSQL
   - Session cookie sent to client (HTTP-only, secure)

2. **Session Management**
   - Every request includes session cookie
   - Server validates session from PostgreSQL
   - User object attached to `req.user`
   - Session expires after inactivity

3. **Logout**
   - Server destroys session
   - Client cookie cleared
   - User redirected to login

### Authorization (RBAC)

#### Role Hierarchy
```
system_admin (Highest privilege)
  └─ Full system configuration access
     └─ User management
     └─ System settings
     └─ Device configuration

hr_manager
  └─ Complete HR operations

     └─ Leave approval

     └─ Payroll processing
     └─ Recruitment

department_manager
  └─ Team management

     └─ Team expense approval

     └─ Employee requests

employee (Base access)

```

#### Middleware Implementation
```typescript
// Backend: server/routes.ts
function requireRole(...allowedRoles: string[]) {
  return (req, res, next) => {
    if (!req.user) {
      return res.status(401).json({ message: "Not authenticated" });
    }
    if (!allowedRoles.includes(req.user.role)) {
      return res.status(403).json({ message: "Insufficient permissions" });
    }
    next();
  };
}

// Usage
app.post("/api/employees", requireRole("hr_manager", "system_admin"), ...);
```

```typescript
// Frontend: client/src/components/RequireRole.tsx
export function RequireRole({ 
  allowedRoles, 
  children 
}: { 
  allowedRoles: string[], 
  children: React.ReactNode 
}) {
  const { user } = useAuth();
  
  if (!user || !allowedRoles.includes(user.role)) {
    return <Navigate to="/" />;
  }
  
  return <>{children}</>;
}

// Usage in routes
<Route path="/admin/users">
  {() => (
    <RequireRole allowedRoles={["system_admin"]}>
      <UserManagement />
    </RequireRole>
  )}
</Route>
```

```typescript
export const myNewTable = pgTable("my_new_table", {
  id: varchar("id").primaryKey().default(sql`gen_random_uuid()`),
  name: text("name").notNull(),
  createdAt: timestamp("created_at").defaultNow().notNull(),
});

// Generate Zod schema for validation
export const insertMyNewTableSchema = createInsertSchema(myNewTable).omit({
  id: true,
  createdAt: true,
});

// TypeScript types
export type InsertMyNewTable = z.infer<typeof insertMyNewTableSchema>;
export type SelectMyNewTable = typeof myNewTable.$inferSelect;
```

#### 2. Push Schema to Database
```bash
npm run db:push
```

#### 3. Create API Routes
Edit `server/routes.ts`:
```typescript
app.get("/api/my-resource", async (req, res) => {
  const results = await storage.getMyResources();
  res.json(results);
});

app.post("/api/my-resource", requireRole("hr_manager"), async (req, res) => {
  const validatedData = insertMyNewTableSchema.parse(req.body);
  const created = await storage.createMyResource(validatedData);
  res.status(201).json(created);
});
```

#### 4. Update Storage Interface
Edit `server/storage.ts`:
```typescript
interface IStorage {
  // ... existing methods
  getMyResources(): Promise<SelectMyNewTable[]>;
  createMyResource(data: InsertMyNewTable): Promise<SelectMyNewTable>;
}
```

```typescript
import { useQuery, useMutation } from "@tanstack/react-query";
import { apiRequest, queryClient } from "@/lib/queryClient";

export default function MyFeature() {
  const { data, isLoading } = useQuery({
    queryKey: ["/api/my-resource"],
  });
  
  const createMutation = useMutation({
    mutationFn: (data: InsertMyNewTable) =>
      apiRequest("/api/my-resource", "POST", data),
    onSuccess: () => {
      queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ["/api/my-resource"] });
    },
  });
  
  return <div>Your UI here</div>;
}
```

#### 6. Add Route
Edit `client/src/App.tsx`:
```typescript
import MyFeature from "@/pages/my-feature";

// In Router component:
<Route path="/my-feature" component={MyFeature} />
```

#### 7. Add Navigation
Edit `client/src/components/app-sidebar.tsx`:
```typescript
{
  title: "My Feature",
  url: "/my-feature",
  icon: IconComponent,
}
```

### Coding Standards

#### TypeScript
- Strict mode enabled
- No `any` types (use `unknown` if necessary)
- Explicit return types for functions
- Interface for object shapes

#### React
- Functional components only
- Custom hooks for reusable logic

- Memoization for expensive computations

#### CSS/Tailwind

### Testing Strategy

**Recommended Testing Approach:**
1. **Unit Tests**: Vitest for utility functions
2. **Integration Tests**: API route testing with Supertest
3. **E2E Tests**: Playwright for critical user flows

### Git Workflow

**Branching Strategy:**
- `main`: Production-ready code
- `develop`: Integration branch
- `feature/*`: New features
- `bugfix/*`: Bug fixes
- `hotfix/*`: Urgent production fixes

**Commit Convention:**

## Performance Optimization

# HRMS - Quick Start Guide

## For Developers

### 🚀 Get Up and Running in 5 Minutes

#### Step 1: Prerequisites Check
```bash
# Check Node.js version (need 18+)
node --version

# Check npm version
npm --version

# Verify PostgreSQL access (optional - can use Neon)
psql --version
```

#### Step 2: Clone and Install

```bash
# Clone the repository
git clone <repository-url>
cd hrms-project

# Install all dependencies
npm install
```

#### Step 3: Database Setup

**Option A: Using Neon (Recommended)**
1. Sign up at https://neon.tech
2. Create a new project
3. Copy the connection string

**Option B: Local PostgreSQL**
```bash
# Create database
createdb hrms_development
```

#### Step 4: Environment Configuration

Create `.env` file in project root:

```bash
# Database
DATABASE_URL=postgresql://user:password@host:5432/dbname
PGHOST=your-host.neon.tech
PGDATABASE=hrms_development
PGUSER=your_username
PGPASSWORD=your_password
PGPORT=5432

# Session (generate random string)
SESSION_SECRET=generate-random-32-char-string-here

# Email (get from resend.com)
RESEND_API_KEY=re_your_api_key_here
```

**Generating SESSION_SECRET:**
```bash
# On macOS/Linux
openssl rand -base64 32

# Or in Node.js
node -e "console.log(require('crypto').randomBytes(32).toString('base64'))"
```

#### Step 5: Initialize Database
```bash
# Push schema to database
npm run db:push
```

You should see:
```
✓ Applying changes
✓ Schema pushed successfully
```

#### Step 6: Start Development Server
```bash
npm run dev
```

Expected output:
```
VITE v5.4.20  ready in 1234 ms

  ➜  Local:   http://localhost:5000/
  ➜  Network: use --host to expose
  ➜  press h + enter to show help

Server running on http://localhost:5000
```

#### Step 7: Access the Application

1. Open browser to `http://localhost:5000`
2. You'll see the landing page
3. Click "Login"

#### Step 8: Create First Admin User

**Important:** You need to create the first user directly in the database.

```sql
-- Connect to your database
psql $DATABASE_URL

-- Or use a database client (TablePlus, pgAdmin, etc.)

-- Create first admin user
INSERT INTO users (email, first_name, last_name, password_hash, role)
VALUES (
  'admin@company.com',
  'System',
  'Admin',
  '$2b$10$abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz123456789',  -- temporary, will change on login
  'system_admin'
);
```

**Better Option: Use Node.js Script**

Create `scripts/create-admin.ts`:
```typescript
import bcrypt from 'bcrypt';
import { drizzle } from 'drizzle-orm/neon-serverless';
import { neonConfig, Pool } from '@neondatabase/serverless';
import { users } from '../shared/schema';

neonConfig.fetchConnectionCache = true;

const pool = new Pool({ connectionString: process.env.DATABASE_URL });
const db = drizzle(pool);

async function createAdmin() {
  const password = 'admin123'; // Change after first login!
  const passwordHash = await bcrypt.hash(password, 10);
  
  await db.insert(users).values({
    email: 'admin@company.com',
    firstName: 'System',
    lastName: 'Admin',
    passwordHash,
    role: 'system_admin',
  });
  
  console.log('Admin user created!');
  console.log('Email: admin@company.com');
  console.log('Password: admin123');
  console.log('Please change password after first login!');
  process.exit(0);
}

createAdmin();
```

Run it:
```bash
tsx scripts/create-admin.ts
```

#### Step 9: Login and Configure

1. Login with admin credentials
2. Navigate to `/admin/departments`
3. Create your first department (e.g., "Engineering")
4. Navigate to `/admin/leave-types`
5. Create leave types (e.g., "Sick Leave" - 10 days)
6. Navigate to `/admin/expense-categories`
7. Create expense categories (e.g., "Travel")
8. Navigate to `/admin/users`
9. Create additional users

#### Step 10: Test the System

**Create a test employee:**
1. Navigate to `/employees`
2. Click "Add Employee"
3. Fill in details
4. Submit

**Test leave request:**
1. Navigate to `/leave`
2. Click "Request Leave"
3. Select dates and submit
4. Switch to admin/manager account
5. Navigate to `/leave-approval`
6. Approve the request

**Test attendance:**
1. Navigate to `/attendance-entry`
2. Enter manual attendance
3. View in `/attendance`

---

## For System Administrators

### Initial System Setup (Non-Technical)

#### 1. Access Your HRMS Instance
- Your IT team will provide you with the URL
- Default admin credentials will be sent via email

#### 2. First Login
1. Open the HRMS URL in your browser
2. Enter your email and temporary password
3. You'll be prompted to change your password
4. Choose a strong password (minimum 8 characters)

#### 3. Configure Departments
1. Click on "Admin Dashboard" in the sidebar
2. Navigate to "Departments"
3. Click "Add Department"
4. Enter department names one by one:
   - Engineering
   - Sales
   - Marketing
   - Finance
   - Human Resources
   - Operations
5. Click "Save" after each entry

#### 4. Set Up Leave Types
1. Navigate to "Leave Types" in admin menu
2. Add common leave types:
   - **Sick Leave**: 10 days per year
   - **Annual Leave**: 20 days per year
   - **Casual Leave**: 5 days per year
   - **Maternity Leave**: 90 days per year (if applicable)
   - **Paternity Leave**: 15 days per year (if applicable)
3. Click "Save" after each entry

#### 5. Configure Expense Categories
1. Navigate to "Expense Categories"
2. Add categories relevant to your organization:
   - Travel
   - Meals & Entertainment
   - Accommodation
   - Office Supplies
   - Training & Development
   - Communication
3. Click "Save" after each entry

#### 6. Create User Accounts
1. Navigate to "User Management"
2. Click "Add User"
3. For each employee:
   - Enter their email address
   - Enter first and last name
   - Select their role:
     - **System Admin**: For IT staff
     - **HR Manager**: For HR team
     - **Department Manager**: For team leads
     - **Employee**: For all other staff
   - Select their department
4. Click "Create User"
5. System will:
   - Generate a temporary password
   - Send credentials via email
   - User will change password on first login

#### 7. Set Up Attendance Devices (If Applicable)

**If you have ZKTeco biometric devices:**

1. Navigate to "Device Configuration"
2. Click "Add Device"
3. For each device:
   - **Device Name**: e.g., "Main Office Entry"
   - **IP Address**: Ask your IT team (e.g., 192.168.1.100)
   - **Port**: Usually 4370 (default)
   - **Location**: e.g., "Reception Desk"
   - **Branch**: Your office location
4. Click "Save"
5. Click "Test Connection" to verify device is reachable
6. If connection succeeds, click "Sync Now" to import existing attendance data

**If you don't have biometric devices:**
- Users can manually enter attendance via `/attendance-entry`
- Managers can enter attendance for their team members

#### 8. Train Your Team

**For HR Managers:**
- Show them how to approve leave requests
- Demonstrate expense approval process
- Teach them recruitment module for job postings
- Show payroll processing workflow

**For Department Managers:**
- Explain how to approve team leave
- Show expense approval for their department
- Demonstrate performance review process

**For Employees:**
- How to request leave
- How to submit expense claims
- How to view attendance
- How to set performance goals

#### 9. Communicate Rollout

Send company-wide email with:
- HRMS URL
- What each employee needs to do (check email for credentials)
- Training schedule
- Support contact (you!)
- FAQ document

```
Error: Unable to connect to database
```

**Solution:**
- Check DATABASE_URL is correct
- Verify database exists
- Check network/firewall allows connection
- For Neon: Verify project is not sleeping

### Issue 2: Session Not Persisting
```
User keeps getting logged out
```

**Solution:**
- Verify SESSION_SECRET is set
- Check that sessions table exists in database
- Ensure cookies are enabled in browser

### Issue 3: Email Not Sending
```
User creation succeeds but no email received
```

**Solution:**
- Verify RESEND_API_KEY is correct
- Check Resend domain is verified
- Look for emails in spam folder
- Check Resend dashboard for errors

### Issue 4: Device Connection Failed
```

```

**Solution:**
- Verify device is powered on
- Check IP address is correct
- Ensure device and server are on same network
- Verify port 4370 is open (not blocked by firewall)
- Try pinging the device IP from server

### Issue 5: Cannot Create First Admin
```
No admin account exists to login
```

**Solution:**
- Use the create-admin script (see Step 8 above)

### Attendance Module

#### Features
- **Attendance Records**: View daily check-in/check-out times
- **Calendar View**: Visual attendance calendar
- **Filters**: 
  - Time Period (Today, This Week, This Month, Custom Range)
  - Department
  - Location
  - Company/Branch

#### How to Use Filters
1. Select time period from dropdown
2. For custom range, select "Custom Range" and pick dates
3. Select department (if you have access to multiple)
4. Select location/branch
5. Click "Apply Filters"
6. Click "Reset Filters" to clear

#### Understanding Attendance Data
- **Check-in Time**: When employee arrived
- **Check-out Time**: When employee left
- **Total Hours**: Automatically calculated
- **Device**: Which biometric device recorded the attendance

---

### Leave Module

#### Leave Types
Common leave types:
- **Sick Leave**: For illness or medical appointments
- **Annual Leave**: Vacation or personal time
- **Casual Leave**: Short-term personal needs
- **Maternity/Paternity Leave**: For new parents

#### Leave Request Workflow
```
Employee Submits Request
         ↓
Manager Reviews Request
         ↓
   Approved / Rejected
         ↓
Email Notification to Employee
```

#### Leave Balance Calculation
- Balance = Days Allowed - Days Used - Days Pending
- Resets annually (company policy)

### Expense Module

#### Expense Categories
Common categories:
- **Travel**: Transportation, mileage, flights
- **Meals**: Business meals, client dinners
- **Accommodation**: Hotel stays
- **Supplies**: Office supplies, equipment
- **Other**: Miscellaneous business expenses

#### Best Practices for Expense Claims
1. **Always upload receipts** for claims over $50
2. **Submit promptly** (within 30 days of expense)
3. **Be specific** in descriptions
4. **Categorize correctly**
5. **Include client/project** information if applicable

#### Components
1. **Performance Goals**: Individual objectives
2. **Appraisals**: Formal performance reviews
3. **Feedback**: 360-degree feedback from peers/managers

#### Setting SMART Goals
- **S**pecific: Clearly defined
- **M**easurable: Quantifiable progress
- **A**chievable: Realistic
- **R**elevant: Aligned with job role
- **T**ime-bound: Has a deadline

#### Example Goals
- "Complete certification course by Q1 2025" (Progress: 75%)
- "Improve customer satisfaction score to 4.5/5" (Progress: 60%)
- "Lead 2 successful project launches" (Progress: 50%)

2. View recent notifications
3. Click notification to navigate to related item

1. Navigate to relevant module (Reports, Attendance, etc.)
2. Click "Export" button
3. Select format (CSV or PDF)
4. File downloads automatically

## FAQs

### General

**Q: I forgot my password. What should I do?**
A: Contact your System Administrator to reset your password. They will send you a new temporary password via email.

**Q: Can I access HRMS on my mobile device?**
A: Yes! The system is fully responsive and works on smartphones and tablets.

**Q: How do I switch between light and dark mode?**
A: Click your profile icon, select "Theme", and choose your preferred mode.

### Attendance

**Q: Why isn't my attendance showing up?**
A: If using biometric devices, ensure you've registered your biometric ID. Contact HR if your ID is not configured.

**Q: Can I edit my attendance records?**
A: No, attendance records from biometric devices cannot be edited. For corrections, contact your HR Manager.

**Q: What if I forget to check out?**
A: Your manager can manually enter your check-out time via the attendance entry feature.

### Leave

**Q: How many leave days do I have?**
A: View your leave balance on the Leave page. It shows remaining days for each leave type.

**Q: Can I cancel a submitted leave request?**
A: Not directly. Contact your manager to cancel a pending request.

**Q: When will I know if my leave is approved?**
A: You'll receive an email notification once your manager approves or rejects your request.

### Expenses

**Q: What expenses can I claim?**
A: Any legitimate business expense. Common categories include Travel, Meals, Accommodation, and Supplies.

**Q: Do I need to upload receipts?**
A: Yes, always upload receipts for verification. Claims without receipts may be rejected.

**Q: How long does expense approval take?**
A: Typically 2-5 business days, depending on your manager's availability.

### Performance

**Q: How often should I update my goal progress?**
A: Update weekly or monthly to keep stakeholders informed.

**Q: Who can see my performance goals?**
A: Your manager and HR can view your goals. Peers cannot see them unless you share.

**Q: When will I receive my performance appraisal?**
A: Appraisals are typically conducted quarterly or annually, depending on company policy.

### Technical Issues

**Q: The page isn't loading. What should I do?**
A: Try refreshing your browser. If the issue persists, clear your cache or contact IT support.

**Q: I'm getting a "Permission Denied" error.**
A: You're trying to access a feature not available to your role. Contact your System Administrator if you believe this is incorrect.

**Q: Can I use multiple browser tabs?**
A: Yes, but be aware that logging out in one tab will log you out in all tabs.

---

- **System Admin**: For account and access issues
- **HR Manager**: For leave, expenses, and employee-related queries
- **IT Support**: For technical problems

### Training Resources
- Review this user guide
- Attend onboarding sessions
- Request one-on-one training from HR

Job posting creation and management - Candidate application tracking - Interview stage progression (Applied → Screening → Interview → Offer → Hired) - Candidate notes and history ### 📊 Reports & Analytics - Department configuration - Leave type and expense category setup - Automated credential emails via Resend --- ## Quick Start ### Prerequisites - Node.js 18+ and npm - PostgreSQL database (Neon recommended) - Open browser to `http://localhost:5000` - Default admin credentials will be created on first run --- ## Documentation Comprehensive documentation is available in the `/docs` folder: 📖 **[Technical Documentation](docs/TECHNICAL_DOCUMENTATION.md)** -
